title: Fix stuck bead infinite skip loop

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
When a bead exceeds stuck_bead_threshold, it's skipped but never closed or deprioritized. beads.Ready() returns the same stuck bead on the next iteration, creating an infinite loop of 'Skipped after N failures' logs with duplicate comments added each time. Loops until maxIterations.

Fix: After skipping a stuck bead, call beads.ReadyAny() or track skipped IDs in a set to get the NEXT bead instead. If all beads are stuck, exit the loop cleanly with a message.

Acceptance criteria:
- Stuck beads are skipped exactly once per run, not re-fetched
- If all ready beads are stuck, loop exits with clear message
- No duplicate comments added to stuck beads

title: Add ralph triage command to refine ideas into tasks
description:
Add `ralph triage` command to interactively review backlog and promote ideas to real beads.

## Usage
```bash
ralph triage              # Interactive triage session
ralph triage <idea-id>    # Triage a specific idea
```

## Interactive flow
For each idea:
1. Display the idea and any context
2. Ask: "What needs to happen to complete this?" (refine into actionable task)
3. Ask: "Priority?" [0=critical, 1=normal, 2=low] 
4. Ask: "Any dependencies or related tasks?"
5. Ask: "Expected outputs?" (optional, for progress tracking)
6. Create the bead via bd
7. Remove from backlog
8. Ask: "Next idea? [y/n]"

## Example session
```
Triaging: idea-003 [feature] What if we had a web dashboard?

What needs to happen to complete this?
> Create a simple web UI that shows ralph run history and current status

Priority? [0/1/2, default=1]: 2

Any dependencies? (bead IDs, comma-separated, or skip): 

Expected outputs? (files, comma-separated, or skip):
> internal/web/server.go, internal/web/handlers.go

✓ Created bead ralph-runner-xyz: Create web UI for run history and status
✓ Removed idea-003 from backlog

Next idea? [y/n]: n
```

- cmd/ralph/triage.go
- internal/backlog/backlog.go (add Remove method)

title: Standardize JSON extraction from LLM output into shared utility

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
Three different JSON extraction strategies exist:
1. ParseScopeEstimate (prompt.go) -- first '{' to last '}'
2. parseAnalysisOutput (analyzer.go) -- same first/last bracket approach
3. ParseProposals (proposals.go) -- regex for fenced code blocks
4. parseDecomposeOutput (runner.go) -- raw Unmarshal, no extraction

Create a shared utility (e.g. internal/llmjson/extract.go) that tries:
1. Extract from fenced code block (most robust)
2. Fall back to bracket matching
3. Fall back to raw unmarshal

Then use it in all four call sites.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single ExtractJSON(output string, target any) function
- Used by all four parsers
- Tests cover: pure JSON, code-fenced JSON, JSON with surrounding text, arrays and objects
- Existing tests still pass

Key files: internal/prompt/prompt.go, internal/analyzer/analyzer.go, internal/retro/proposals.go, internal/runner/runner.go

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
The core loop (processBead, retry/escalation, stuck bead skipping, decomposition) has zero test coverage. TestRetryCounterBehavior is a no-op.

Depends on: ralph-runner-thd (interfaces for testability)

Write integration tests using mock dependencies:
1. Happy path: bead fetched, claude succeeds, validation passes, bead closed
2. Retry path: claude fails, retried on same model, succeeds
3. Escalation path: claude fails, escalates haiku->sonnet->opus
4. Stuck bead path: bead exceeds threshold, skipped
5. Decomposition path: all models exhausted, decompose triggers

Also: delete TestRetryCounterBehavior (the no-op documentary test).

title: Detect and display partial progress on failure
description:
When validation fails, show what work was actually done to help diagnose the issue.

## Requirements

### 1. Git diff summary (always)
When validation fails, show git diff summary:
```
Validation failed. Changes detected:
  internal/retro/retro.go    | 142 +++++++++++
  cmd/ralph/main.go          |  38 ++-
  2 files changed, 178 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

This immediately tells you 'Claude did work, something else broke' vs 'Claude did nothing.'

### 2. Expected outputs checklist (optional)
If bead spec includes `expected_outputs:` field, show checklist:
```
Expected outputs:
  ✓ internal/retro/retro.go (created)
  ✓ cmd/ralph/main.go (modified)
  ✗ internal/retro/retro_test.go (not found)
  ✗ .ralph/templates/PROMPT_retro.md (not found)
```

Add optional `expected_outputs` field to bead specs:
```yaml
expected_outputs:
  - internal/retro/retro.go
  - internal/retro/retro_test.go
  - .ralph/templates/PROMPT_retro.md
```

## Implementation notes
- Git diff: run `git diff --stat HEAD` after validation fails
- Track git HEAD at task start to compare against
- Expected outputs: parse from bead description or add structured field

title: Add pre-flight environment checks
description:
Before running validation, verify required tools are available. Offer to install if missing.

## Requirements

### 1. Parse required tools from validation commands
Extract tool names from `validation.commands` in ralph.yaml:
- `go test ./...` → requires `go`
- `npm run build` → requires `npm`
- `mise exec -- go build` → requires `mise` and `go`

### 2. Check tool availability
Before validation, verify each tool exists:
```
Pre-flight check:
  ✓ go (1.25.7)
  ✓ mise (2024.12.0)
```

### 3. Prompt to install if missing (default behavior)
```
Pre-flight check:
  ✗ go not found

go is required for validation. Options:
  [1] Run 'mise install' (mise.toml detected)
  [2] Skip validation and continue
  [3] Abort

Choice [1]:
```

### 4. Configuration in ralph.yaml
```yaml
preflight:
  auto_install: ask    # ask | always | never
  tools:               # optional explicit list
    - go
    - mise
```

- `ask` (default): Prompt user before installing
- `always`: Auto-run mise install / npm install without asking  
- `never`: Just fail with clear error message

## Implementation notes
- Detect mise.toml / .tool-versions for mise install
- Detect package.json for npm/pnpm install
- Detect go.mod for go mod download
- Use `which` or `command -v` to check tool availability

## Files to modify
- internal/runner/runner.go (add preflight check step)
- internal/config/config.go (add PreflightConfig struct)
- ralph.yaml (document new config options)

title: SECURITY: Fix path traversal in spec file loading
description:
CRITICAL: Path traversal vulnerability in spec file loading.

## Issue
`internal/prompt/prompt.go:98-107` builds file paths without validating spec name:
```go
path := filepath.Join(r.specsDir, name+".md")
```

A malicious bead label like `spec:../../../../../../etc/passwd` could read files outside specs directory.

## Fix
- Validate spec names against path traversal characters (`..`, `/`, `\`)
- Use `filepath.Clean()` and verify result stays within specsDir
- Reject any name containing suspicious patterns

## Files
- internal/prompt/prompt.go

title: Add ralph add command for idea capture
description:
Add `ralph add` command to quickly capture ideas to the backlog.

## Usage
```bash
ralph add "Add cost tracking"
ralph add "Fix the auth bug" 
ralph add "What if we had a web dashboard?"
```

## Behavior
1. Takes a single string argument (the idea)
2. Optionally asks 1-2 clarifying questions to categorize:
   - Is this a feature, bug, or chore? (auto-detect if obvious)
   - Any additional context? (optional, can skip)
3. Saves to backlog storage (NOT beads yet)
4. Prints confirmation: "Added to backlog: <idea>"

## Storage
Create `.ralph/backlog.jsonl` with entries like:
```json
{"id": "idea-001", "text": "Add cost tracking", "type": "feature", "context": "", "created_at": "..."}
```

## Auto-categorization heuristics
- Contains "fix", "bug", "broken", "error" → bug
- Contains "add", "implement", "create", "new" → feature  
- Contains "refactor", "clean", "update", "upgrade" → chore
- Otherwise → ask

## Files to create
- cmd/ralph/add.go
- internal/backlog/backlog.go (storage layer)

title: Add visibility with streaming and heartbeat
description:
Add real-time visibility into what Claude is doing during task execution.

## Requirements

### 1. Full firehose streaming to file
- Stream all Claude tool calls and responses to `.ralph/logs/stream-{timestamp}.log`
- User can `tail -f` this file to see everything in real-time
- Format: timestamp + event type + summary
```
[12:34:56] TOOL_CALL: Read /internal/runner/runner.go
[12:34:58] TOOL_RESULT: 245 lines read
[12:35:02] TOOL_CALL: Edit /internal/runner/runner.go (lines 42-58)
[12:35:04] TOOL_RESULT: Edit successful
```

### 2. Periodic heartbeat in terminal
- Every 60 seconds, print a status summary to terminal
- Shows: elapsed time, files modified, tool calls made
```
[2m elapsed] Still working. 3 files modified, 12 tool calls.
[3m elapsed] Still working. 5 files modified, 23 tool calls.
```

### 3. Stream file path shown at start
```
Running Claude with model: sonnet
Streaming to: .ralph/logs/stream-20260205-143000.log (tail -f to watch)
```

## Implementation notes
- May need to intercept/wrap Claude CLI output
- Consider using Claude's `--output-format` if available
- Heartbeat should not interrupt Claude's work, just print status

description: In cmd/gromit/install_skill.go, the claudeSettings struct (line 52) only declares a Hooks field. title: Add deadline check to runner loop

title: Write comprehensive README.md
description:
Create a great README.md that explains ralph-runner clearly and gets people excited to use it.

## Sections to include

### Hero section
- Clear one-liner: what is ralph-runner?
- Why it exists (the Ralph Wiggum loop problem)
- Quick visual/diagram of the loop if possible (ASCII art)

### Quick start
- Installation
- `ralph init` to set up a project
- `ralph run` to start processing beads
- Show example output

### How it works
- The loop: get bead → run Claude → validate → close or escalate
- Model selection (P0=opus, P1=sonnet, P2=haiku)
- Escalation chain on failure
- Fresh context each iteration (the key insight)

### Self-improvement system
- LEARNINGS.md - provisional vs confirmed
- RULES.md - project constraints
- `ralph retro` - analyze and consolidate
- Smart retro suggestions

### Configuration
- ralph.yaml reference
- Model selection by priority/labels
- Validation commands
- Pre-flight checks
- Paths

### Reliability features
- Validation output capture
- Streaming + heartbeat (tail -f)
- Partial progress detection (git diff)
- Pre-flight environment checks

### Integration with bd (beads)
- How beads work
- Creating beads for ralph
- Expected outputs field

### Philosophy
- Why fresh context matters
- Why learnings beat fine-tuning
- The human-in-the-loop retro

## Tone
- Practical, not academic
- Show don't tell (examples > explanations)
- A little personality is ok

## Files to create/modify
- README.md (create or overwrite)

title: Ensure trailing newline after heartbeat overwrite before next log output
description:
In internal/runner/runner.go, the overwriteHeartbeat function (line 712) writes with fmt.Fprintf(r.output, "\r%s%s", newLine, padding) - no trailing newline. This is intentional for in-place overwriting, but when the heartbeat goroutine is stopped and the next r.log() call happens, there's no newline separating the heartbeat line from the next log message.

The heartbeat goroutine runs concurrently with Claude's streaming output (both writing to r.output), which can also cause interleaved output.

Fix: When stopHeartbeat() is called (heartbeat goroutine exits), ensure the output has a trailing newline if the last heartbeat used overwrite mode. Consider adding synchronization or ensuring a newline is written when the heartbeat goroutine is shutting down.

Acceptance criteria:
1. After heartbeat stops, the next r.log call starts on a fresh line
2. No visual artifacts from overwritten heartbeat lines remain in output

title: Ensure trailing newline after Claude streaming output

title: Change constructors to return (T, error) instead of nil

comments.author: Dan Abrams
comments.text:
NewRunner, NewRetro, and NewAnalyzer return nil on invalid input instead of (*T, error). This forces every caller to check for nil AND causes the nil guard proliferation -- every method defensively checks fields that should be guaranteed non-nil by construction.

Change these constructors to return (*T, error):
- NewRunner(cfg, output) -> (*Runner, error)
- NewRetro(ralphDir, cfg) -> (*Retro, error)  
- NewAnalyzer(renderer, claude, templateDir) -> (*Analyzer, error)

Then remove the redundant nil field checks from methods (the triplicated 5-field block in Run/processBead/DecomposeTask).

Acceptance criteria:
- All three constructors return (*T, error)
- Callers updated to handle error return
- Redundant nil field checks removed from methods
- All tests pass
